newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain and China endorse HK's container terminal.
newsitem.headline: Britain and China endorse HK's container terminal.

text.p: Britain and China have endorsed an agreement on the construction of Container Terminal Number Nine (CT9), the government radio said.
Consensus had been reached and a statement would be made on Thursday, it quoted the Secretary of Constitutional Affairs Nicholas Ng as saying.
"The agreement is understood to involve the Jardines led consortium swaping its berths for those now operated by Modern Terminal off Stonecutters Island," the radio said.

Jardine originally led the Tsing Yi consortium and was awarded the CT9 contract through a private treaty granted to them and two other consortia led by Wharf (Holdings) Ltd , and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd in 1992.
But Beijing refused to give the project its approval because the contract straddles the handover next year, citing the lack of an open tender.

Beijing also accused the Hong Kong government of rewarding Jardine, a pillar of the British establishment since the colony was founded, for supporting Governor Chris Patten's electoral reforms, themselves the object of bitter Chinese opposition.
The new agreement disbanded the Jardine-led consortium and replaced it with a consortium to be named Asia Container Terminals (ACT), the South China Morning Post said.

Shareholders in the new consortium remained unchanged but its forerunner Jardine was replaced by the more politically acceptable Sea-Land Orient Terminals as leader of the group, the newspaper quoted sources as saying.
Jardine's stake would be the second largest behind Sea-Land in the new consortium, it added.
